clue.text: Delight in some description of a poet's garden

parts.note: delight, as a verb, means to love something

explanation.surface: Taking pleasure in the way a poet once pictured his garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is T. E. Brown, whose poem opens 'A garden is a lovesome thing, God wot!'; 'Delight' looks like the definition but is only the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lovely or pleasing, the very word a Victorian poet famously used for his garden.

clue.text: 3's words when, written may lead to action

definitions.text: 3's words when, written may lead to action

parts.words: 3's words when, written may lead to action
parts.note: a defamer's spoken words, once committed to paper, become a written defamation that can bring a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Things a defamer says can end in court when put on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is the answer at 3-down, a slanderer; 'action' is a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Written defamatory statements are the published form of what a slanderer speaks.

clue.text: There's a point in every sort of hunting

indicators.note: the point sits in the middle of the other letters
to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Every kind of hunt has a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges EVERY to VEERY, and 'in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venery is an old word for the chase, the sport of hunting game.

clue.text: Cuban, for example, without one word of hesitation, is an utterly evil type

indicators.note: without means taking away the named letter

parts.note: a Cuban is one example of an islander

explanation.surface: A Cuban who speaks without hesitating is a wicked person.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: one who utters evil, not someone utterly wicked. 'without' takes I from ISLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanderer spreads malicious falsehoods, literally a speaker of ill about others.

clue.text: Fresh lament on men making fire-station superstructures

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: A new complaint about firemen leads to building works at the fire station.
explanation.walkthrough: The fire station is the fireplace, where the fire is stationed; 'on' places one piece by the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantelpiece is the shelf and frame built above a fireplace.

clue.text: Italian island is to honour Indian Army leaders

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: the leaders of the words Indian and Army are their first letters

explanation.surface: An Italian island pays tribute to the commanders of the Indian Army.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour often used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, belonging to Italy.

clue.text: Lighter fall

definitions.meaning: a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire
to tumble or overturn something, as in tipping out a drink

explanation.definitionFit: A taper for lighting a pipe has the same name as a tumble from a horse.

clue.text: Tune Hugo composed, the French Calvinist

indicators.note: composed suggests the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Victor Hugo writes a melody for a French Protestant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges TUNE and HUGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Huguenots were French Protestants who followed the teachings of Calvin.

clue.text: Drug trial? Conclusive proof

definitions.meaning: a test of the drug LSD, known as acid
a decisive test of worth, from the use of acid to test gold

explanation.definitionFit: Acid was used to prove gold genuine, giving a phrase for a decisive check, and acid is slang for LSD.

clue.text: Strip girl's handkerchief

parts.note: a strip of material is a band

explanation.surface: A strip of cloth belonging to a girl serves as her hanky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a verb, as in undressing, but it is the noun band.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large patterned handkerchief, often worn round the neck or head.

clue.text: An antelope — nothing exotically gay

parts.note: gai is the French for gay, so gay put in a foreign tongue

explanation.surface: An antelope that is nothing like as bright and cheerful as it might be abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotically' asks for the foreign word: French gai for gay.
explanation.definitionFit: The nilgai is a large Indian antelope, also called the blue bull.

clue.text: Cases in Latin composition one counts as defective

parts.note: prose is a schoolboy translation into Latin

indicators.note: something defective is faulty, so these letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Schoolboy Latin exercises in which one's sums are wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: A prose is a translation exercise into Latin or Greek; 'as defective' rearranges I and COUNTS to CUTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosecutions are legal cases brought against defendants.

clue.text: Fifty-one died besieging the old city. Ghastly!

indicators.note: letters besieging others surround them, as an army surrounds a town

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Fifty-one people perished during the siege of an ancient city: horrifying!
explanation.walkthrough: 'besieging' puts UR inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes something shocking and gruesome in detail, just as horrible things are.

clue.text: Left me on rent-revision registration

indicators.note: a revision rewrites things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is left out of a rent review form and has to sign up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges L, ME, ON and RENT; 'rent-revision' reads as one landlord's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing on or being entered on a register.

clue.text: Nothing in purse perhaps to cover bill? Quite absurd!

indicators.note: letters that cover others enclose them on either side
perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged some other way

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck up on a wall

explanation.surface: An empty purse, perhaps, to pay a bill: utterly ridiculous!
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges O and PURSE into PREOUS, whose two halves go either side of the bill; 'in' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Preposterous means utterly absurd, contrary to reason.

clue.text: She sees eagles on the point

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point

explanation.surface: A woman watches eagles perched on the headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like a headland, but it is a prong; 'sees' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name is defined by the pronoun standing for any female.

clue.text: Bleach for each kind of leather (hydrogen extracted)

indicators.note: the named element is extracted, taken away

parts.note: oxhide is leather made from the skin of an ox
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A bleaching agent for every type of leather, once hydrogen is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted' takes H out of OXHIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen peroxide is a common bleaching agent, especially for hair.

clue.text: Pretended to be attacked

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both feigned, as a manner, and struck down by illness.

clue.text: Bubbly has effects never otherwise apparent

indicators.note: the letters appear otherwise, in a different order

explanation.surface: Champagne has effects that would never show up any other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise apparent' rearranges EFFECTS and NEVER; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Effervescent means fizzing with bubbles, or lively, like champagne.

clue.text: Harry makes girl, return south

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: Harry gets a girl to head back south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester or persistently attack them.

clue.text: Feast, weight-watchers try to prevent

definitions.meaning: a lavish meal laid out on the table

explanation.definitionFit: A lavish meal is laid out on the table, and a thickening waistline is what dieters fear.

clue.text: Second writer, restricted by patent, got into red

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in inside it

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A second author, hampered by a patent dispute, ended up in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' is the adjective meaning obvious, not the inventor's licence; 'restricted by' puts S and the writer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending more than you have puts your account in the red, in debt.

clue.text: Disease caused by herb, odds on

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds at a race's start

explanation.surface: An illness caused by a herb, odds-on to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprue is a tropical disease of the digestive tract.

clue.text: Frank shows the way with the current measure

parts.note: the amp is the unit measuring electric current

explanation.surface: Frank demonstrates the route alongside a measurement of the stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' is the verb, to frank a letter, not a name or honest.
explanation.definitionFit: To frank a letter is to mark it with a postage stamp or postmark.

clue.text: Fashionable bird? Shut up!

explanation.surface: Someone tells a trendy bird to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like a call for silence, but it is the verb to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to confine them, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Landlord looks healthy, from what I hear

indicators.note: the phrase tells us the words are to be heard spoken

parts.note: a bonny face is a healthy-looking one

explanation.surface: The pub landlord seems in good health, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Boniface is the innkeeper in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem, so the name came to mean any landlord; 'bonny' is British for pretty and healthy-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a stage innkeeper became a byword for a publican or innkeeper.

clue.text: Supplied fee at last

indicators.note: the fee is placed at, that is within, the last

parts.note: the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Someone finally provided the fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like a phrase meaning finally, but 'last' gives a word for the end and 'at' sets the fee within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to provide or furnish someone with a quality.

clue.text: What 3 did in itself — terribly sad all round

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go all round the other piece
terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: per se is Latin for in itself

explanation.surface: What a defamer did was, in itself, dreadfully sad from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 refers to the answer at 3-down, the defamer; 'terribly' turns the three letters into ASD, which splits round the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanderer casts aspersions, attacking a reputation with false charges.
